<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" />{{rh|408|THE EPISTLE OF S. PAVL|CHA. X.}}</noinclude>beleeueth. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=5}}† For Moyses vvrote, {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Lev. 18, 5.''}}* that, the iustice vvhich is of the Lavv, {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ The iustice of the Law of Moyses went no further of it self, but to saue a man from the temporal death and punishment prescribed to the transgressors of the same.}}∷ ''the man that hath done it, shal liue in it''. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=6}}† But {{sup|‖}} the iustice vvhich is of faith, saith thus, {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Deu. 30, 12.''}}* ''Say not in thy hart, Vvho shal ascend into heauen''? that is to bring Christ dovvne. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=7}}† ''Or vvho descendeth into the depth''? that is to call Christ againe from the dead. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=8}}† But vvhat saith the Scripture? ''The vvord is nigh, in thy mouth, and in thy hart''. this is {{sup|‖}} the vvord of faith vvhich vve preach. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=9}}† For if thou confesse vvith thy mouth our Lord {{sc|Iesvs}}, and in thy hart beleeue that God hath raised him vp from the dead, thou shalt be saued. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=10}}† {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=The Epistle vpō S. Andrewes day, Nouemb. 30.}}For vvith the hart vve beleeue vnto iustice: but vvith the mouth confession is made to saluation. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=11}}† For the Scripture saith: {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Esa. 28, 16.''}}* ''Vvhosoeuer beleeueth in him, shal not be confounded''. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=12}}† For there is no distinction of the Iew and the Greeke: for one is Lord of al, riche tovvard al that inuocate him. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=13}}† {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Ioel. 2, 22.''}}* ''For euery one '' {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ To beleeue in him & to inuocate him, is to serue him with al loue and sincere affectiō. Al that so doe, shal doubtlesse be saued & shal neuer be confounded.}}∷ ''vvhosoeuer shal inuocate the name of our Lord, shal be saued''. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=14}}† {{sup|‖}} Hovv then shal they inuocate in vvhom they haue not beleeued? Or hovv shal they beleeue him vvhom they haue not heard? And hovv shal they heare without a preacher? {{verse|chapter=10|verse=15}}† But hovv shal they preach {{sup|‖}} vnles they be sent? as it is vvritten: {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Esa. 52, 7.''}}* ''Hovv beautiful are the feete of them that euangelize peace, of them that euangelize good things''? {{verse|chapter=10|verse=16}}† But al {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Esa. 53, 1.''}}* do not obey the Gospel. For Esay saith, Lord, vvho hath beleeued the hearing of vs? {{verse|chapter=10|verse=17}}† Faith then, is by hearing: and heating is by the vvord of Christ. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=18}}† But I say, haue they not heard? And certes {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Ps. 18, 5.''}}* ''into al the earth hath the sound of them gone forth: and vnto the endes of the vvhole vvorld the vvordes of them''.⊣

{{verse|chapter=10|verse=19}}† But I say, hath not Israel knovven? Moyses first saith, {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Deu. 32, 21.''}}* ''I vvil bring you to emulation in that vvhich is not a nation: in a folish nation I vvil driue you into anger''. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=20}}† But Esay is bold, and saith, {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Esa. 65, 1.''}}* ''I vvas found of them that did not seeke me: openly I appeared to them{{sup|‖}} {{sup|‖}} that asked not of me''. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=21}}† But to Israel he saith, {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Esa. 65, 2.''}}* ''Al the day haue I spred my handes to a people that beleeueth not, and contradicteth me''.

{{c|{{larger|A N N O T A T I O N S}}}}
{{c|{{sc|Chap. X.}}}}

''3. The iustice of God.''] {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=Gods iustice, & the Iewes owne iustice.}}The iustice of God, is that which God giueth vs through Christ. the Ievves owne or proper iustice, is that which they had or chalenged to haue of them selues and by their ovvne strength, holpen onely by the knovvledge of the Law without the helpe or grace of Christ.

''6. The iustice of faith.''] {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=Iustice of faith.}}The iustice which is of faith, reacheth to the life to come, making man assured of the truth of such Articles as concerne the same. as, of Christs Ascension to heauen, of his Descending to Hel, of his comming downe, to be Incarnate, and his Resurrection and returne againe to be glorified: by which his actions we be pardoned, iustified, and saued, as by the Law we could neuer be.<noinclude>{{continues|''8. The''}}</noinclude>
